
# load data
```{r}
csv_name = "jen-SRaging.csv"
raw_df = read.csv(paste(data_dir, csv_name, sep = "/"),
                   header = T) %>%

plot_df = raw_df %>% 
  mutate(weight = 1/`var_ppi_VS.VS_c14_2mm_model.Fwin.Floss_Swin.Sloss_type.ppi_seed.VS_cope.14_cname.rew.pun_F.S`) %>% 
  rename(DV = `ppi_VS.VS_c14_2mm_model.Fwin.Floss_Swin.Sloss_type.ppi_seed.VS_cope.14_cname.rew.pun_F.S`,
         IV_focal = age_demeaned,
         ctrl_tsnr = avg_tsnr_demeaned,
         ctrl_fdmean = avg_fdmean_demeaned,
         ctrl_study = study_demeaned,
         ctrl_flip = flip_demeaned,
         )
```


# figure data prep
```{r}
# 3. Partial out the control variable 'A' from 'Y' using WLS
model_y_on_a <- lm(Y ~ A, data = df, weights = C)
df$y_resid <- residuals(model_y_on_a)

# 4. Partial out the control variable 'A' from 'X' using WLS
model_x_on_a <- lm(X ~ A, data = df, weights = C)
df$x_resid <- residuals(model_x_on_a)

# 5. Create the partial residual plot
ggplot(df, aes(x = x_resid, y = y_resid)) +
  # Plot the partial residuals. We can still map size to the original weights.
  geom_point(aes(size = C), color = "darkgreen", alpha = 0.7) +
  
  # Add a weighted regression line through the partial residuals.
  # The slope of this line is the partial coefficient of X.
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", aes(weight = C), color = "black", se = FALSE) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Partial Residual Plot for X",
    subtitle = "Visualizing the weighted relationship between Y and X, after controlling for A",
    x = "Residuals of X ~ A (X | A)",
    y = "Residuals of Y ~ A (Y | A)",
    size = "Weight (C)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# (Optional) Prove that the slope is identical to the coefficient in the full model
full_wls_model <- lm(Y ~ X + A, data = df, weights = C)
partial_plot_model <- lm(y_resid ~ x_resid, data = df, weights = C)

print("Coefficient for X in full model:")
print(coef(full_wls_model)["X"])

print("Coefficient for x_resid in partial plot model:")
print(coef(partial_plot_model)["x_resid"])

```
